sentences.text: Myledaphus is an extinct genus of guitarfish.
The genus was first described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1876.
Remains found in both marine and freshwater deposits suggest Myledaphus could tolerate a range of salinity.
The animal possessed blunt, polygonal teeth arranged in a pavement for crushing and grinding hard-bodied prey.
Wear on the teeth indicates Myledaphus fed on mollusks common in Late Cretaceous North American rivers.
It is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Myledaphus belongs to the family Rhinobatidae.
Fossils of this animal date from 93.9 to 61.66 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Danian stages.
Recent research suggests Myledaphus bipartitus should be recovered as a member of Rhinopristiformes.
